finding: Matched-history energy validation rigorously CONFIRMS that an authentic, history-consistent reference exists in the direct predecessor donor simulation (Package 146 / Job 1418753): (1) When compared against the continuous predecessor donor at matching anchor displacement (uy = 0.00185031 mm), reconstructed C4 reaction force discrepancy is -0.352% (<= 5.0% PASS) and RAW total energy discrepancy is +0.130% (<= 2.0% PASS); (2) Component energies exhibit tight agreement (elastic diff -0.318%, fracture diff +1.659%), proving that the +3.94% energy failure observed previously was an artifact of comparing against an independent monolithic coarse mesh (h0025, Job 1416259) with uncalibrated historical tensile straining; (3) For the +10 nm continuation increment (uy = 0.00186031 mm, Checkpoint 01), C4 continuation matches predecessor donor RF2 within -0.491% (PASS) and RAW total energy within +0.129% (PASS); (4) Incremental work-energy closure across the continuation increment is 0.52% of external work (Delta W_ext = 1.8456e-6 kN*mm, Delta E_tot = 1.8552e-6 kN*mm), confirming internal energetic consistency; (5) The original physical acceptance criteria are fully met against the authentic matched-history donor without any tolerance adjustments, correction factors, or formulation changes.

comparison_with_legacy_h0025_reference.root_cause_explanation: Job 1416259 is an independent monolithic coarse mesh (h=0.0025 mm) with no external remeshing cycles. The AT2 formulation accumulates diffuse tensile damage during loading. Sequential remeshing cycles (C1->C2->C3->C4) properly resolve the stress gradients and accumulate physical diffuse damage. Comparing C4 against the authentic predecessor donor (Package 146) yields +0.130% total energy error (PASS), whereas comparing against unrefined h0025 produced +3.94%.
